Graduate Programs
Master of Science
The Master of Science program is a broad-based curriculum designed to prepare students for advanced positions in the computing industry as well as for further academic studies. The M.S. degree requires a minimum of 30 credit hours of graduate-level coursework.
The Master of Science in computer science is available via distance learning.
Doctor of Philosophy
The doctorate degree program is a research-oriented curriculum designed to prepare students for the advanced research industry and university-level academic positions in the computing field.
Application information
Minimum admission requirements
All students must supply a personal statement (explaining why they want to pursue graduate studies), a resume, and three reference letters. Their background should include (as documented by transcripts) either:
a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science (or a closely related field) from an accredited institution in the United States, with a GPA of at least 3.0, or
a degree from an institution outside the United States that is comparable to a US degree as mentioned above, along with Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores which should be at least 146 Verbal, 151 Quantitative, 3.0 Analytical Writing.
International students who received their degree(s) abroad must take a language test approved by the university, typically (though TOEFL is also common) the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) where a score of at least 6.5 is required.
Applicants from certain English-speaking countries are exempt from this requirement.
K-State's codes for the TOEFL: Institution Code: 6334, Department Code: 78
Application deadlines
Fall – January 8th prior to Fall start.
Spring – August 1st prior to Spring start.
